llm.summary: This is a clearly described paid XMTP lead-generation skill, with disclosed payments, group access, monitoring, and invite behavior, but users should treat it as a high-impact commercial integration.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires wallet/XMTP identity, ERC-8004 registration, USDC payments, and adding Basemate to a group with member-add permissions; these are proportionate to the service but carry payment, privacy, and outreach implications.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains documentation and JSON service cards only; no executable installer, local scripts, dependency installation, or local code execution path was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The DM flow uses broad phrases such as subscribe, buy humans, cph, and lead subscribe, but they are presented as messages sent directly to Basemate and the flow asks for interests, group ID, price, and confirmation before setup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Subscriptions and Basemate group membership are ongoing service state; this is disclosed, but users should verify active cancellation controls and remove Basemate from groups when no longer needed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is pay-per-human lead generation for XMTP groups, and the documented capabilities align with that purpose: subscriptions, USDC/x402 payments, intent matching, and invite DMs to matched users.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want Basemate to participate in your XMTP group, process matched group-message activity through its service, send invite DMs to potential leads, and use USDC payments. Confirm the target group, per-human price, setup fee, cancellation process, and privacy/compliance terms before authorizing subscriptions or delivery claims.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Confirmed the generic DM trigger phrases in SKILL.md; they are part of an explicit Basemate DM subscription flow with follow-up questions and confirmation, so this is a user-control caution rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Confirmed the skill discloses monitoring opted-in XMTP groups and GPT-4o-mini intent scoring; retention, access, and compliance details are not specified, so users should review privacy terms before use.
[SQP-1] expected: Confirmed MCP tools can subscribe, check status, discover groups, and claim paid deliveries; the payment annotations and purpose are clear, though agents should require explicit user approval before invoking paid or externally visible actions.
